blurb: A derived capability, `capability Name = Kind`, takes its configuration from options after the kind, and some kinds cannot work without them: a `Service` needs the Worker it reaches, `@worker(…)`, a `Queue` its `@name(…)`, a `RateLimit` its `@limit(…)` and `@period(…)`, and a `StoredSecret` its `@store(…)` and `@secret(…)`. There is no default. Write the options the note shows. A value the platform would refuse is `bynk.capability.invalid_option`; an option the kind does not take is `bynk.capability.unknown_option`.
summary: A derived capability lacks an option its base requires, such as a `Service` instance's `@worker`.
